description: Activity History V1 — cross-client, append-only Quartzo history for user-visible object, occurrence, capture, organization, manual execution, tracking, and focus events.

scope.canonicalMeaning: Activity is Quartzo activity shared between clients. It is not limited to Obsidian-local plugin actions.
scope.navigation: Activity is a primary Companion shell surface beside Home, Planner, Journal, and Browse.
nonGoals: do not reconstruct full history from filesystem mtime
do not store UI analytics or clicks
do not create a second object index
do not expose unsupported Canvas activity in V1

persistence.recordFormat: One canonical ActivityEvent JSON object per line.
rules: eventId is stable and deterministic for a completed operation
replaying the same operationId and eventType must not append a duplicate event
events are appended only after the owning operation has completed
sync conflicts must preserve all distinct eventIds
clients must never mutate source objects only to record activity
history starts when this contract is active; clients must not backfill invented events from mtime

requiredFields.occurredAt: ISO-8601 instant when the owning operation completed.
requiredFields.sourceId: Canonical object, occurrence, routine, system, tracking, capture, or focus source ID.
requiredFields.sourcePath: Vault-relative source path when a file-backed source exists.
requiredFields.originClient: Stable client identifier such as quartzo_app or obsidian_companion.
requiredFields.originKind: One of app, companion, import, sync, automation, or external_integration.
requiredFields.titleSnapshot: Short title captured at event time.

optionalFields.excerpt: Privacy-gated preview; never a full diff or full note body.
optionalFields.previousPath: Previous vault-relative path when the event moved or renamed a file.
optionalFields.changedFieldCount: Integer count of changed semantic fields when known.
optionalFields.operationId: Owning operation id used for idempotency.
optionalFields.scheduledFor: Canonical local date for scheduled occurrence events.
optionalFields.folder: Derived folder path used for folder filters.
optionalFields.provenance: Real provider/source metadata when known; absent when unknown.
optionalFields.metadata: Event-type-specific metadata; must not contain secrets.

ownerBoundaries.rule: Activity events are emitted by canonical operation owners after confirmed mutation or runtime completion, never by UI surfaces.

privacy.excerptPolicy: Excerpt is optional and privacy-gated. Clients may omit it without weakening the event.
rules: do not persist full note bodies or diffs
do not persist excerpts from private or sensitive fields
privacy mode must suppress excerpt rendering
metadata must describe the event without exposing secrets
provider labels are shown only from real provenance

projection.singleOwner: Clients must use one Activity History reader/projection owner. UI surfaces must not maintain independent counts.
rules: all counts, groups, charts, heatmaps, folder buckets, and totals are derived from the same filtered projection
Day aggregation uses hourly buckets for the selected local day
Week aggregation uses daily buckets across the selected week and may include recent-week context
Month aggregation must represent days or weeks in the selected month, not a mislabeled 12-month heatmap
Year aggregation must represent all twelve months or real daily/year buckets, not a short fake heatmap
unsupported event categories must be hidden or disabled, never rendered with fake events

filters.folderFilter: Vault-relative folder prefix or all folders.

dateNavigation.day: plus or minus one local day
dateNavigation.week: plus or minus one ISO week
dateNavigation.month: plus or minus one calendar month
dateNavigation.year: plus or minus one calendar year

rules: period and filter controls expose selected state
timeline events are keyboard reachable when they have a target
heatmap and chart buckets expose date/range and count labels
stat bars expose textual value equivalents
loading, empty, filtered-empty, stale/offline, and error states are distinct
